program_name: Bachelor in Sustainable Agriculture and Forestry in Mountain Environments
teaching_language: Trilingual (Italian / German / English). The admission information states verbatim: 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English.' Weighting in practice (unibz 'Course Offering - Enrolled from 2025' listing for both semesters, checked 2026-08-29): approximately 7 courses in Italian, 7 in English and 5 in German. Italian and English are tied as the largest teaching languages and German is a close third, so no single language dominates. Crucially, several compulsory core courses are offered in one language only and have no English alternative: Fundamentals of Chemistry, Fundamentals of Agricultural and Forest Engineering, Informatics, General Arboriculture, Rural Appraisal and Marketing for the Agricultural and Forestry Sector, Biology of Microorganisms of Agricultural and Forestry Interest and Agricultural and Forestry Mechanization are Italian-only; Plant and Animal Biology, Sustainable Animal Husbandry and Grassland Management, Fundamentals of Soil Science and Soil Chemistry and Fundamentals of Agricultural and Forestry Economics and Policy are German-only. English-taught core courses are Mathematics and Applied Statistics, Fundamentals of Plant Production, Biochemistry and Plant Physiology and Entomology and Phytopathology. The programme therefore cannot be completed in English alone. English is proportionally weaker here than in the unibz engineering bachelors, because the Italian- and German-only blocks cover both the basic-science and the applied-agronomy backbone. [uncertain]
campus: Bozen-Bolzano (main campus). Faculty of Agricultural, Environmental and Food Sciences, Universitaetsplatz 5 / piazza Universita 5, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano, Italy. Single campus - no Brixen-Bressanone, Bruneck-Brunico, NOI Techpark, Trento or Innsbruck component. Teaching is combined with practical exercises and fieldwork carried out in South Tyrol, and the compulsory internship (minimum 150 hours) may be done at Italian or foreign partner businesses.
degree_class: L-25 (Scienze e tecnologie agrarie e forestali / Agricultural and Forestry Sciences and Technologies). 180 ECTS, 3 years full time. Brochure 'At a glance': 'Bachelor class: L-25, ECTS credits: 180, Duration of the course: 3 years'. The degree gives access to the State Examination for the National Register of Chartered Agronomists and Foresters (Section B).
offered_in_2026_27: Yes - actively offered and recruiting for 2026/27, and still open at the verification date. All three EU sessions plus the non-EU session ran: signed ranking lists were published for the Early Bird session (24 EU admitted, 2 non-EU admitted) and for the Late session (10 EU admitted), and the programme is explicitly listed as 'Application possible' in the Additional Application Session (application window 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04, ranking by 2026-09-18). The admission information PDF carries 'Latest update: 20.08.2026'. Not suspended, unlike Wood Technology and Tourism Management. Because both earlier sessions filled only 34 of the 70 EU places, the Additional Session is a genuine live opportunity rather than a formality.
is_new_programme: Not a new programme in substance, but new in name and structure. It is the renamed and restructured continuation of an existing L-25 bachelor at the same university, not a first-intake programme. Naming chain: the 2019/20 Study Manifesto shows 'Corso di laurea in Scienze agrarie, degli Alimenti e dell'Ambiente montano' (English: Agricultural, Food and Mountain Environmental Sciences) under the then Faculty of Science and Technology, campus Bolzano, class L-25, 70 EU + 5 non-EU places; the English name used in the intervening years was 'Bachelor in Agricultural and Agro-Environmental Sciences', which still appears as the heading of the unrevised Grade Statistics L-25 page under the current programme URL; the present name is 'Sustainable Agriculture and Forestry in Mountain Environments' / 'Agricoltura sostenibile e Gestione forestale in Ambiente montano'. The old slug bachelor-agriculture-food-sciences-mountain-environment still resolves and now displays the new name, confirming a rename rather than a new accreditation. The restructured curriculum (two majors, 15 ECTS free choice, 6 CP internship, 6 CP thesis) applies to the cohort labelled 'Enrolled from 2025' - the only cohort tab on the course-offering page - which places the first intake under the new name and study plan in academic year 2025/26. The faculty itself was created in the March 2023 reorganisation that split the former Faculty of Science and Technology. The exact decree and academic year of the name change are not stated on any official unibz page. [uncertain]
majors_tracks_study_plans: Two majors, chosen in the third year, on a single common study plan for years 1 and 2. Brochure verbatim: 'Two majors allow students to specialise'. (1) Sustainable agricultural production - 'in-depth study of topics such as fruit growing and viticulture, livestock breeding and husbandry, arable farming, sustainable pest management and irrigation techniques'; third-year modules include Fundamentals of Hydrology and Irrigation (10 CP), Fundamentals of Plant Protection (10 CP), Sustainable Animal and Crop Production in Mountain Areas (10 CP) and Fruit Production and Viticulture (10 CP). (2) Management of Forest Environments - 'focus on forest ecology, forest management, protection of mountain ecosystems, hydrology and water management measures for the protection of the territory'; third-year modules include Fundamentals of Hydrology and Irrigation (10 CP), Fundamentals of Forest Ecosystem Ecology (11 CP), Forestry (11 CP, Silviculture + Forest Mensuration) and Function, Protection and Sustainability of Mountain Ecosystems (8 CP). Common to both: 'The three-year course begins with two years of joint basic studies'; both majors carry 6 CP Internship, 10 CP Free Choice in year 3 (plus 5 CP Free Choice in year 1, 15 ECTS elective in total) and 6 CP Bachelor Thesis. Brochure note: 'During the 3rd year of studies students have to choose between one of the following paths' and 'Students can choose free choice courses both internally as well as externally.' There is no dual-study variant, no part-time plan and no separate admission route per major - applicants are admitted to the programme, not to a major.
english_only_accessibility: effectively-closed. A candidate who knows only English cannot be admitted. Entry requires B2 in the FIRST language AND B2 in the SECOND language, drawn from German, Italian and English; English alone fills only the first slot, so a second B2 in German or Italian is mandatory. The ranking decree states the rule directly: admission presupposes B2 competence 'in almeno due delle tre lingue di insegnamento (tedesco, italiano, inglese)' and those who cannot prove it 'vengono escluse dalla procedura di ammissione'. The 2026/27 ranking lists quantify the barrier: in the Early Bird session 15 EU-track candidates and 4 of the 6 non-EU applicants living abroad were excluded solely for failing the language requirement, and in the Late session a further 15 candidates were excluded on the same ground - more people were excluded for language than were admitted in the Late session. Two important qualifications distinguish this programme from the unibz engineering bachelors, where every non-EU applicant was excluded: (a) 2 non-EU applicants living abroad WERE admitted in Early Bird 2026/27, with scores of 14.69 and 12.72 out of 15, so the non-EU route demonstrably works for candidates who hold the second language; (b) two candidates excluded for language in Early Bird (applicant IDs 152198 and 144319) reappear as admitted in the Late session, showing that the bar can be cleared between sessions by obtaining the missing certificate. Even after admission the curriculum is not English-only - seven compulsory courses are Italian-only and four German-only - and graduation demands C1/C1/B2 across all three languages. A Turkish applicant with English only should treat this programme as closed unless a recognised B2 in German or Italian is already held or can be obtained by the application deadline.
admission_type: restricted access (numerus clausus) with merit-based ranking on school records - NO entrance exam, NO test, NO interview. This is the key structural difference from the unibz engineering bachelors: there is no unibz admission exam, no TOLC-I and no CENT-S. Fixed places: 70 for EU citizens and persons given parity of treatment (50 Early Bird + 20 Late) and 4 for non-EU citizens living abroad. A language-requirement check acts as a hard pre-filter before ranking. Selection is a documents-only evaluation worth a maximum of 15 points, built entirely from upper-secondary school grades that the candidate self-certifies in the application portal. Verbatim: 'The evaluation procedure is based exclusively on the documents submitted by the candidate when submitting the application via the relevant portal.'
academic_requirements: Secondary school leaving certificate from the Italian system, or an equivalent qualification obtained abroad. Verbatim: 'Foreign school leaving certificates are considered equivalent if obtained after 12 years of education. In this case, you furthermore must have attended at least the last two years in the foreign school system (e.g. Irish Leaving Certificate: it is not enough to attend one year and obtain the foreign certificate).' The Italian Ministry of Education, University and Research imposes extra requirements on holders of certain certificates (explicitly named: American high school diplomas, British and Greek certificates) - candidates must contact apply@unibz.it (Advisory Service). Applicants must also satisfy the language requirements or they are excluded from the procedure. Subject-specific expectation, stated under Additional educational requirements: 'For this programme an adequate initial preparation in mathematics, physics, chemistry and biology is required. Initial preparation is verified through school records.' No ECTS/SSD credit prerequisites apply - that regime concerns master programmes. National rule: simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 study programmes is allowed, provided they are not in the same degree class (e.g. not L-18/L-18) and differ in at least 2/3 of the course contents. A Turkish 'Lise Diplomasi' meets the 12-year rule but must be accompanied by ARDI/CIMEA documentation (see credential_recognition), and Turkish-language school report cards must be officially translated (see required_documents).
entry_exam_or_test: None. There is no entrance examination of any kind for this programme - no unibz admission exam, no TOLC-I, no CENT-S, no SAT and no subject test. The admission information PDF contains no exam date, and the signed ranking decrees list only a documents-based score out of 15. This is a substantive difference from the 2019/20 predecessor programme, whose Study Manifesto still listed a 'test d'ingresso' alongside the school-record evaluation ('Procedura di selezione: Valutazione del rendimento scolastico e test d'ingresso'); the current regime has dropped the test and kept only the school-record evaluation. The only scheduled assessments an applicant may need to sit are the unibz Language Centre language exams (online, B2 level only), which prove language proficiency rather than academic aptitude: 2026-03-16 (registration 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-09); 2026-04-16, 2026-04-17, 2026-04-20 and 2026-04-21 (registration 2026-03-24 to 2026-04-08); 2026-06-22 to 2026-06-26 for the Late session (registration 2026-05-28 to 2026-06-15). No language exams are offered during the Additional Application Session, so applicants in that window must already hold a recognised certificate. Separately, an OFA remedial exam in mathematics and/or chemistry may be imposed AFTER admission (see ofa_rules).
selection_scoring: Documents-only rubric, maximum 15 points, verbatim: 'Candidates can obtain a maximum of 15 points: up to 5 points for the average of the grades obtained in the third-last and penultimate year of upper secondary school. Grades in behaviour, religion and physical education will not be taken into account. up to 5 points for the average of the mathematics grades. up to 5 points for the average of biology, physics and chemistry grades.' Tie-break: 'In the event of a tie, priority is given to the youngest candidate.' Missing-data rules are published: if a candidate fails to indicate the final grades of the third-last and penultimate year, 'the Commission will assign a final grade equal to the pass mark to the school year for which the prospective student has not produced any certification'; for candidates from school systems without those report cards, 'the Commission reserves the right to evaluate any high school report cards provided by the candidate for school years other than the penultimate and third last.' No minimum pass mark or cut-off score is published - the only score-linked consequence is the OFA trigger at an average of 3 or below in the two science components (see ofa_rules), and admission is decided purely by rank against the available places. No grade-point-average requirement applies (that regime belongs to master programmes such as Software Engineering 24/30). Actual 2026/27 competition, from the signed decrees: Early Bird EU admitted scores ran from 14.45 down to 3.48 with 24 of 50 places taken; the non-EU list had just 2 admitted at 14.69 and 12.72; the Late session admitted 10 with scores from 14.79 down to 5.00. A score in the low single digits was sufficient in both EU sessions, so on score alone this is one of the least competitive unibz bachelors - the binding filter is language, not merit. The absence of a published minimum threshold is inferred from the admission PDF and both signed ranking decrees, neither of which mentions one. [uncertain]
bonus_points: None. The rubric is exhaustive and closed at 15 points across exactly three school-grade components. There is no Webometrics university-ranking bonus (that applies to the Master in Software Engineering and the Master in Computing for Data Science), no GMAT/GRE bonus (Master in Accounting and Finance), no start-up project bonus (Master in Entrepreneurship and Innovation), no bonus for work experience, competitions, olympiads or agricultural background, and no bonus for South Tyrolean residence. Age functions only as a tie-breaker, not as points.
portfolio_and_materials: None required. No portfolio, no video, no project proposal, no motivation letter, no CV and no reference letters are requested - unlike Design and Art, Critical Creative Practices or Eco-Social Design. The format limits published for those programmes (portfolio max 20 MB PDF, project proposal max 2 A4, motivation letter max 6,000 characters, video max 2 minutes) do not apply here. What must be uploaded instead is quantitative school evidence: self-certified final grades for the third-last and penultimate year of upper secondary school entered directly in the portal, plus scanned report cards for candidates who completed those years abroad, plus an official translation of the report cards into Italian, German or English where needed. Verbatim: 'Those who have completed the relevant years abroad must upload a copy of the relevant report cards to the portal.' The report cards are effectively this programme's equivalent of a portfolio, and 'Candidates must upload the required documents to the admission portal, under penalty of automatic exclusion from the process.'
interview: No interview. Selection is entirely documents-based; the Admission Commission evaluates only the material uploaded to the portal by the application deadline. Verbatim: 'The commission will only consider the documents uploaded to the portal by the application deadline.' No interview dates are published for this programme, and none appear in either signed ranking decree. The Commission does retain discretion in two narrow places - assigning a pass-mark default where grades are missing, and deciding which alternative school years to evaluate for non-Italian systems - but exercises it on paper, without meeting the candidate.
conditional_admission: Applicants who have not yet obtained their secondary school diploma may apply: 'If you gained your qualification abroad, you must also upload the diploma of your qualification: if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment.' Until the required foreign-qualification documents are supplied the candidate is admitted 'solo con riserva' (only with reservation), the reservation being lifted once unibz validates the qualification; 'if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.' A separate reservation applies to non-EU citizens living abroad regardless of diploma status: the Early Bird decree records that they 'sono ammessi e ammesse con riserva: la riserva viene sciolta previa comunicazione ufficiale, inviata direttamente all'unibz, dal consolato italiano all'estero' - the reservation is released only when the Italian consulate abroad notifies unibz directly. Financial protection: the first instalment is refunded only if the candidate fails the secondary school final exam, or - for non-EU applicants living abroad - does not obtain the documents needed for enrolment from the Italian authorities. There is NO ECTS-based conditional admission (the 120/140 ECTS rule applies to master programmes), and no late-enrolment window to 11/12/2026 is published for this bachelor. [uncertain]
ofa_rules: OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning requirements) applies, and here it is triggered by school grades rather than by an entrance test. Verbatim: 'To be admitted to the course without being assigned OFA, a minimum grade point average of 3 must be achieved in mathematics and a minimum grade point average of 3 must be achieved in biology, physics and chemistry: students who obtain 3 points or less for the evaluation of the average grade in mathematics are assigned additional training obligations in Mathematics. students who obtain 3 points or less for the evaluation of the average grade in biology, physics and chemistry are assigned additional training obligations in Chemistry.' The two OFAs are independent, so a candidate can receive one, both or neither. Note the wording is self-contradictory at the margin ('a minimum of 3 must be achieved' versus '3 points or less' triggering OFA), so a score of exactly 3 should be assumed to trigger the OFA. Fulfilment: 'The additional learning requirements are fulfilled by passing a specific exam. Additional courses are offered to review basic concepts in mathematics and/or chemistry.' Consequence of failure: 'Students who do not fulfil the additional learning requirements within the first year can enrol in the second year of study, but will not be able to take exams in the second and third years of study.' A mathematics pre-course runs 2026-09-21 to 2026-10-09 to support this. This is a different mechanism from the entrance-test-percentage OFA used by the engineering bachelors and from the mandatory-maths-test OFA used by Economics and Management, Economics Politics and Ethics and Tourism Sport and Event Management.
language_requirements: Trilingual regime with a hard two-language entry bar. Entry: B2 in the first language AND B2 in the second language; no level required in the third language at entry. The three languages are German, Italian and English - 'Your first language is the language in which you have the highest level of proficiency (B2 or C1). Your third language is instead the language in which you are weaker (or in which you are an absolute beginner).' Failure to prove the required levels means exclusion from the admission procedure: 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure.' Certification is mandatory for the first and second language and recommended (from B1 upwards) for the third. B1 in the third language is the minimum for sitting curricular exams held in that language; if the first semester is taught only in English and English is the applicant's third language, at least B1 English must be certified by mid-January. Exit (to graduate): C1 first language, C1 second language, B2 third language. CEFR levels apply throughout. Free Language Centre courses support the third language (target B1 by end of year 1, B2 by end of year 2), delivered as extensive courses of 4 hours per week during semesters and intensive courses of 6 hours per day between semesters. Unlike the engineering bachelors there is no relaxed dual-study variant at B2/B1 - B2/B2 is the only entry standard here. For an English-only international applicant this is the binding constraint; it excluded 15 EU-track and 4 non-EU applicants in the Early Bird session alone.
entry_levels_by_position: Levels are defined by POSITION, not by which language it is: 1st language B2 / 2nd language B2 / 3rd language no level required. The applicant chooses which of German, Italian and English occupies each position, based on the levels actually certified; the first language is the strongest. A B1 in the third language is required in order to sit curricular examinations taught in that language, and must be certified by mid-January of year 1 if English is the third language and semester 1 is English-only. Only B2-level exams can be booked at the unibz Language Centre ('Please note that you can only register for B2 level exams'), so the Language Centre route can satisfy the second-language slot but cannot by itself produce a C1. Compared with sister programmes: this programme sits at the stricter B2/B2 tier, the same as Computer Science and the full-time engineering plans, and above Electronic and Information Engineering (B2/B1); there is no B2/B1 relaxation available here because no dual-study variant exists. Practical note for this specific curriculum: because the compulsory courses are split roughly evenly across Italian, English and German, the 'third language' is not a peripheral concern - a student will meet German- or Italian-taught compulsory modules from the first year onward.
exit_levels: 1st language C1, 2nd language C1, 3rd language B2. These are graduation requirements, not admission requirements, and they directly gate the degree: a student admitted at B2/B2 must raise both to C1 and additionally reach B2 in the third language before graduating. Verbatim: 'Exit level (to graduate) 1st language: C1, 2nd language: C1, 3rd language: B2.' The Language Centre offers the necessary courses free of charge and sets intermediate milestones for the third language - 'B1 level by the end of the 1st year; B2 level by the end of the 2nd year' - which means the third-language exit level is effectively expected one full year before graduation. For an applicant entering with, say, English C1 and Italian B2, the practical workload is Italian to C1 plus German from zero to B2 over three years.
third_language_exam_threshold: B1 in the third language is the threshold for taking curricular examinations delivered in that language. Verbatim: 'A B1 level in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations in that specific language.' Special case: 'Please note that if the first semester of your study programme is only taught in English and your third language is English, you will have to certify at least a B1 level in English by mid-January to be able to take all the curricular exams scheduled for the first semester.' Students without a third-language certificate sit a placement test after admission ('If you are not able to certify your language competence in the third language and you are admitted to unibz, you will have to take a placement test') and are assigned a learning path aimed at reaching B2 as soon as possible. Absolute beginners must use the September intensive course, because 'Beginner courses (A1) will be offered exclusively during the pre-semester intensive course session in September will no longer be offered during the academic year.' This is a significant trap for Additional Session applicants, who are admitted too late to attend the September intensive courses.
proof_pathways: Four accepted routes to prove language proficiency. (1) The main teaching language of the final high school year, if German, Italian or English - recognised as C1 (Ladin upper secondary schools: recognised as B2 in German and Italian). For foreign qualifications, 'If the main teaching language is not clearly stated on your high school diploma, please also upload a letter/document issued by your high school stating the medium of instruction.' (2) A bachelor or master degree taught in Italian, German or English - recognised as C1; unibz graduates upload their certificates or declare Language Centre exams passed (B2, B2+ or C1); foreign degrees need a university letter stating the medium of instruction if not on the diploma. (3) A recognised language certificate from the official unibz list (https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf); 'If you cannot upload the certificates, you can send them by e-mail as PDF files or deliver them in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline.' (4) A language exam organised by the unibz Language Centre, booked online through the application portal under 'enrol for language exams' after creating the application - 'you can only register for B2 level exams.' 2026/27 online language exam dates and registration windows: 2026-03-16 (registration 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-09); 2026-04-16, 2026-04-17, 2026-04-20 and 2026-04-21 (registration 2026-03-24 to 2026-04-08); 2026-06-22 to 2026-06-26 for the Late session (registration 2026-05-28 to 2026-06-15). No Language Centre exams are offered during the Additional Application Session. If the application is started outside a registration window the applicant must return to the portal during one of these windows. Additional route for bilingual/multilingual and foreign secondary schools: 'If the foreign language proficiency levels (for German, Italian, or English) are explicitly indicated on the diploma of graduation according to the Common European Framework of Reference (i.e., B1, B2 or C1), and if all four language abilities (reading, listening, speaking, writing) have been assessed, then the indicated levels will be accepted as a proof of proficiency for the second and/or third language' - subject to Language Centre approval. Certificates from Italian public institutions require a self-declaration; those from foreign public institutions require a scanned copy of the original.
certificate_rules: Governed by Resolution of the University Council n. 16/2026 ('Recognised language certificates and diplomas'), verified directly in the certificate list PDF on 2026-08-29. Rules, verbatim from the English section: a certificate must include 'the assessment in all four skills and the certificate must be issued by the certification organisation itself' and must indicate adequate performance in all skills in the form of an overall grade. 'If no overall result and/or level is stated on the certificate, the lowest level reached in one of the subskills is decisive for determining the level, provided that this part of the examination has been passed.' 'There is no compensation for "failed" parts of the exam and no averages are calculated unless these provided by the certification organisation.' 'Certificates issued by exam boards and obtained by taking an online exam ("home edition") are not recognised, except for those explicitly indicated in the list' - a handful of entries in the list are footnoted 'Also accepted as "home edition"'. Certificates covering single skills from different organisations are refused; certificates of participation, end-of-course tests, private-institution exams and placement-test results are refused; 'no certificates are recognised that are issued by individual lecturers or teachers' and 'DAAD certificates are not recognised.' Validity: international language certificates must not be older than five years before the date of submission, with the entire calendar year applying from 1 January. Items listed under 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' have unlimited validity. Recognised providers include Goethe-Institut and OeSD for German and the corresponding boards for Italian and English, level by level A2-C2. Note: some secondary sources still cite the superseded Resolution 20/2025; the current list in force is 16/2026.
application_deadline_eu: Three separate sessions for EU citizens and persons given parity of treatment; all cut-offs are at 12:00 noon local time. (1) Early Bird Application: 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28. (2) Late Application (EU only): 2026-05-28 to 2026-07-08. (3) Additional Application Session (EU only, opened by the Faculty in August/September only if places remain, and confirmed open for this programme): 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04. Original unibz notation, DD/MM/YYYY: '02/03 - 28/04/2026', '28/05 - 08/07/2026', '18/08 - 04/09/2026'. Candidates excluded in the first session may reapply in the next one - 'If you are excluded in the first session, you might apply again in the second one' - and the 2026/27 ranking lists show this happening in practice, with two Early Bird language-exclusions returning as admitted in the Late session. Once submitted, an application cannot be modified: 'Once the application has been sent, it cannot be modified. Filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly will not be taken into consideration.' Because only 34 of 70 EU places were filled across the first two sessions, the Additional Session was still live at the verification date of 2026-08-29.
application_deadline_non_eu: One single window for non-EU citizens living abroad: 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28 (12:00 noon local time) - i.e. the Early Bird session only. Verbatim: 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' Non-EU applicants living abroad are excluded from the Late Application and from the Additional Application Session, both of which are explicitly EU-only. A non-refundable EUR 50 application fee applies to this group. Practical consequence for Turkish applicants resident in Turkey: the 2026-04-28 noon deadline is the only chance in the cycle, and the required B2+B2 language proof must already be in hand or booked via a Language Centre exam on 2026-03-16 or 2026-04-16/17/20/21 - the June exam window falls after the non-EU deadline and is therefore useless to this group. Encouragingly, and unlike the unibz engineering bachelors, this route did produce admissions in 2026/27: 2 of the 6 non-EU applicants living abroad were admitted.
parity_of_treatment: Two categories are treated as EU citizens. (1) 'Citizens from Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State'. (2) 'Non-EU citizens with a valid permit to stay in Italy (see article 39, paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998: "permesso di soggiorno" (residence permit) for work, family reasons, political or humanitarian asylum, religious reasons). In this case, you apply directly to the University as described above and must submit a copy of your valid permit to stay. A permit to stay for study reasons or a visa for tourism is not sufficient. If the permit has expired, you must attach a renewal request.' Critical warning: 'Please note that if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin.' This third category is the decisive one for Turkish nationals already living in Italy on a work, family or humanitarian permit - it grants access to the 70-place EU pool, to all three sessions including the still-open Additional Session, and removes the EUR 50 application fee and the Universitaly/visa route. Given that the EU pool was less than half filled in 2026/27, parity-of-treatment status is worth substantially more here than at oversubscribed programmes.
places_quotas: EU citizens and persons given parity of treatment: 50 places in the Early Bird Application + 20 places in the Late Application = 70 total. Non-EU citizens living abroad: 4 places, Early Bird only. Brochure 'At a glance': 'Places available: 70 EU + 4 non-EU'. Additional Application Session: no separate quota - it is opened only if places remain. Unfilled Early Bird places roll over: 'For EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only: any remaining places of the early bird application, will be offered in the late application.' 2026/27 actual outcome: Early Bird admitted 24 EU (of 50) and 2 non-EU (of 4), with no waiting list published in either pool; the Late session admitted 10 EU. Total 36 admitted against 74 nominal places, i.e. the programme filled under half its capacity, which is why the Additional Session opened. Historical comparison: the 2019/20 Study Manifesto for the predecessor programme listed '70 UE + 5 non-UE', so the EU quota has been stable and the non-EU quota was reduced from 5 to 4.
ranking_and_enrolment_dates: Early Bird: ranking list published by 2026-05-27; first instalment of tuition fees (EUR 600, secures the place) by 2026-06-05 12:00 noon; online enrolment 2026-07-10 to 2026-08-06 12:00 noon. Late Application: ranking by 2026-07-30; first instalment by 2026-08-06 12:00 noon; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 2026-08-06 12:00 noon. Additional Session: ranking by 2026-09-18; first instalment by 2026-09-25 12:00 noon; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 2026-09-25 12:00 noon. Missing either the payment or the enrolment deadline means automatic loss of the place: 'If you do not meet this deadline, you will automatically be excluded and the next applicant in the ranking list will be admitted.' A candidate admitted to more than one programme may secure a maximum of 2 programmes by paying the instalment twice. Paying does not confer student status - 'Paying university fees does not confer student status, which is only obtained by enrolling' - and payments are non-refundable except for failure of the secondary school final exam or, for non-EU applicants abroad, failure to obtain the enrolment documents from the Italian authorities. Enrolling early is advised so incomplete documents can be corrected before the deadline. Students transferring from another Italian university must give the Student Office a copy of the transfer application at the start of the academic year. Appeals against the ranking decree may be lodged with the Administrative Court of Bozen within 60 days of publication. Rankings 'are valid only for the academic year for which they were drawn up.'
programme_specific_dates: No admission exam or interview dates exist for this programme - the only programme-linked assessment dates are the Language Centre exams, and the only programme-specific selection milestone is the documents deadline of each application session. Language exams (online, B2 only): 2026-03-16 (registration 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-09); 2026-04-16, 2026-04-17, 2026-04-20, 2026-04-21 (registration 2026-03-24 to 2026-04-08); 2026-06-22 to 2026-06-26 (registration 2026-05-28 to 2026-06-15); none during the Additional Session. Preparatory phase 2026/27: intensive language courses 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-18 (Monday to Friday, 6 h/day); mathematics pre-course 2026-09-21 to 2026-10-09; Freshers Days 2026-09-28 and 2026-09-29. Academic calendar 2026/27: 1st semester classes 2026-09-28 to 2026-12-23, extraordinary exam session 2026-12-10 to 2026-12-23, holidays 2026-12-24 to 2027-01-06, classes resume 2027-01-07 to 2027-01-23, exams 2027-01-25 to 2027-02-20; 2nd semester classes 2027-03-01 to 2027-03-25, holidays 2027-03-26 to 2027-03-29, classes 2027-03-30 to 2027-06-12, extraordinary exam session 2027-05-12 to 2027-05-22, exams 2027-06-14 to 2027-07-10; autumn exam session 2027-08-23 to 2027-09-25. Third-language B1 certification deadline for English-only first semesters: mid-January. Curriculum milestones: major chosen at the start of year 3; compulsory internship of at least 150 hours (6 CP); bachelor thesis 6 CP, experimental in nature.
required_documents: At application: (a) an account on the Application Portal (https://aws.unibz.it/exup) plus a valid ID card or passport, front and back, scanned - 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'; (b) the completed online form with all attachments; (c) the secondary school leaving certificate / diploma - if the qualification was gained abroad and the diploma is not yet issued, it must be uploaded at enrolment instead; (d) THE PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC ITEM: self-certified final grades for the third-last and penultimate year of upper secondary school entered directly in the portal, plus, for candidates who completed those years abroad, scanned copies of the corresponding report cards, plus an official translation of the report cards into Italian, German or English where they are in another language - a Turkish-language karne therefore needs translation; (e) language proof - self-declaration if the certificate was awarded by an Italian public institution, scanned copy of the original if awarded by a foreign public institution, plus (where relevant) a school or university letter stating the medium of instruction; (f) for parity-of-treatment applicants, a copy of the valid Italian permit to stay (or renewal request). At enrolment, for foreign secondary school qualifications: the secondary school diploma; an official translation into Italian (not required for diplomas issued in German or English); and the ARDI and/or CIMEA statements (see credential_recognition). No structured study-career Excel template is required for this bachelor - that upload belongs to master applications. 'Mendacious declarations will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list', and false grade declarations specifically 'will be punished by law and will result in exclusion from the admission ranking'. Applications cannot be modified after submission, and only documents uploaded by the deadline are evaluated.
application_fee: EUR 50, charged only to non-EU citizens living abroad. Verbatim: 'Application fee: EUR 50. The fee is an administration fee and is non-refundable.' EU citizens and persons given parity of treatment - including non-EU nationals holding an Italian work, family, humanitarian, asylum or religious residence permit - pay no application fee.
tuition_or_fees_link: Approximately EUR 1,200 per academic year, in two instalments. Verbatim: 'Fees amount to EUR 1200. 1st instalment (EUR 600): includes the revenue stamp of EUR 16. 2nd instalment (EUR 600): must be paid by March of the following year.' The first instalment is what secures the place after the ranking list is published. 'Delayed payment of the second instalment will result in a fine being levied. If you have not paid the tuition fees, you will be unable to take exams and will not be able to transfer to other universities or other study programmes.' No refund on drop-out, interruption or exclusion. Exemptions: students with a disability recognised under article 3, paragraph 1 of Law No 104/1992 or with a disability of 66% or more (certificate to be handed in at the start of the academic year); foreign students granted a scholarship from the Italian government. Students holding a scholarship from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano receive a refund of the tuition fees. For historical context, the 2019/20 predecessor programme charged EUR 1,347.50 per year, so current fees are slightly lower in nominal terms. Fee pages: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/general-information/fees and https://www.unibz.it/en/applicants/studying-at-unibz
scholarships_grants: Main instrument is the provincial study grant of the Autonomous Province of South Tyrol, administered by the Ufficio per il diritto allo studio universitario / Amt fuer Hochschulfoerderung and awarded on income and merit. unibz states the income-based grant is 'between EUR 1,680 and EUR 6,960 per year', and grant holders additionally 'receive the reimbursement of monies paid for the academic year' (tuition refund). Three provincial instruments exist: ordinary study grants, merit scholarships and grants for fostering postgraduate studies; 'Applications for ordinary and merit study grants must be filled in and sent through the e-government service online', with support available from the South Tyrolean Students Association. Merit route: those who 'after the first year, get an average grade of 27/30 for their exams, are eligible to apply for scholarships based on merit' rather than income. Decisive restriction for international applicants: 'Non-EU students can apply for a study grant only if they have a long-time residence permit or after they have had their residence in South Tyrol for at least one year without interruption' - so a first-year non-EU student arriving on a study visa is effectively excluded in year one and must fund that year privately. Exemption from tuition fees applies to holders of an Italian government scholarship and to students with the recognised disability status described above; foreign students and Italian students living abroad may also apply for scholarships funded by the Ministero degli Affari Esteri. No scholarship specific to the Bachelor in Sustainable Agriculture and Forestry in Mountain Environments is published. Note that the official Study Guide 'Study Grants' page names the grant types but does not itself publish the amounts; the EUR 1,680-6,960 range and the 27/30 merit rule come from the unibz 'Studying at unibz' applicant page.
credential_recognition: For a foreign secondary school qualification, upload at enrolment: the diploma itself plus an official translation into Italian ('not necessary for diplomas issued in German or English'), and then, depending on the education system: (a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, International Baccalaureate, European Baccalaureate - the Statement of Correspondence downloaded from ARDI, the Automatic Recognition Database Italy (https://ardi.cimea.it/en); (b) non-EU countries that are signatories to the Lisbon Convention - the ARDI Statement of Correspondence AND the CIMEA Statement of Verification; (c) non-EU countries that are not signatories of the Lisbon Convention - the CIMEA Statement of Comparability AND the CIMEA Statement of Verification (https://cimea-diplome.it/). Turkey is a signatory of the Lisbon Recognition Convention, so a Turkish applicant falls in category (b): ARDI Statement of Correspondence plus CIMEA Statement of Verification. A Turkish-language diploma additionally requires an official Italian translation, and - specific to this programme - the third-last and penultimate year report cards used for scoring must be officially translated into Italian, German or English at application time, which is earlier than the diploma translation deadline. 'unibz performs the necessary checks on your foreign qualification and in case of doubt reserves the right to request additional documents', and 'if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.' The 180-ECTS evidence requirement mentioned in the field definition applies to master admission and not to this bachelor.
non_eu_visa_process: Sequence for non-EU citizens living abroad: apply in the single Early Bird window (2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28) with the EUR 50 fee; if admitted per the ranking list, secure the place by paying the first instalment (EUR 600) by 2026-06-05 noon; then start the visa application on the Universitaly portal (https://www.universitaly.it/) - 'The application on Universitaly is mandatory, otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol. On Universitaly you can apply for one study programme only.' Admission is provisional until the consulate reports back: the Early Bird decree records that non-EU applicants living abroad are admitted with reservation, released only on official communication sent directly to unibz by the Italian consulate abroad. The Italian diplomatic-consular representation then issues the study visa; unibz stresses that admission does not automatically confer any right to a visa. Proof of financial means: 'you will need at least EUR 800 per month for living (accommodation, food, study materials, leisure, clothing)' excluding tuition, which unibz translates into 'a bachelor programme will cost at least EUR 36,000' (EUR 24,000 for a master), plus health insurance and visa expenses and the roughly EUR 1,200 annual tuition. After arrival: 'By law, you will have to apply for a residence permit within 8 working days since your arrival in Italy' - contact the Advisory Service on arrival, and hand the permesso di soggiorno to the Student Office in person or by e-mail once obtained. Work while studying: 'you will be able to work part-time for no more than 20 hours a week and no more than 1,040 hours per year.' Scholarship caveat: provincial grants require a long-term permit or one uninterrupted year of registered residence in South Tyrol. Refund exception: non-EU applicants abroad who cannot obtain the enrolment documents from the Italian authorities are entitled to a refund of the instalment paid. Reality check for 2026/27: 6 non-EU applicants living abroad applied, 4 were excluded for language and 2 were admitted - so the pathway is narrow but genuinely open, in contrast to the unibz engineering bachelors where all non-EU applicants were excluded.

uncertainty_notes: 1) Academic year: all dates, quotas and fees are the published 2026/27 cycle. As of the verification date (2026-08-29) the Early Bird and Late ranking lists are signed and published, and the Additional Session is live - its application window closes 2026-09-04 and its ranking list is due by 2026-09-18, so the final 2026/27 intake figures are not yet known. Figures for 2027/28 are not published. 2) Programme renaming: unibz publishes no explicit notice of the name change. The chain (Scienze agrarie, degli Alimenti e dell'Ambiente montano -> Agricultural and Agro-Environmental Sciences -> Sustainable Agriculture and Forestry in Mountain Environments) is reconstructed from the 2019/20 Study Manifesto, the still-live legacy URL slug, and the unrevised Grade Statistics L-25 page which still carries the older English name. The inference that the new name and study plan took effect in 2025/26 rests on the course-offering page exposing only one cohort tab, 'Enrolled from 2025'; no decree confirming the year was found. 3) Teaching-language weighting: the 7 IT / 7 EN / 5 DE split comes from the 'Enrolled from 2025' course-offering listing, which unibz explicitly says 'shows the lectures that are currently offered in the two semesters. It does not illustrate the structure of the study programme' - it is a snapshot, not a full-curriculum count, and third-year major-specific courses are under-represented in it. Language allocation can change by cohort and by major. 4) Selection threshold: no minimum pass mark is published; the absence is inferred from the admission PDF and both signed ranking decrees. The observed admitted-score floors (3.48 Early Bird, 5.00 Late) are outcomes of undersubscription, not published cut-offs, and must not be treated as a guaranteed bar for future cycles. 5) OFA wording is internally inconsistent at the boundary: the text requires 'a minimum grade point average of 3' yet assigns OFA to those obtaining '3 points or less', so a score of exactly 3 is ambiguous and has been read here as triggering the OFA. 6) Official call: unibz publishes no English-language bando for bachelor programmes, and a programme-specific Regolamento didattico / Studienordnung under the current name was not locatable in any language. 7) Conditional admission: the reservation mechanism is documented, but no ECTS-based conditional admission and no late-enrolment window are published for this bachelor; the description is assembled from the general enrolment rules. 8) URL slug traps: the CoursesPDF slug ('bachelor-in-sustainable-agriculture-and-forestry-in-mountain-environments') differs from the page slug, and the two 2026/27 ranking-list files themselves use inconsistent slugs ('Bachelor-Sustainable-...' vs 'Bachelor-in-Sustainable-...'); a scraper assuming one convention will 404. 9) Scholarship figures: the official Study Guide 'Study Grants' page does not publish amounts; the EUR 1,680-6,960 range and 27/30 merit rule were taken from the 'Studying at unibz' applicant page and are not programme-specific. 10) Non-EU reality check, stated positively: unlike the unibz engineering bachelors, this programme did admit non-EU applicants living abroad in 2026/27 (2 of 6), so the nominal 4 non-EU places represent a real if narrow opening - but 4 of the 6 applicants were still rejected on the two-language B2 requirement, which remains the decisive filter for English-only candidates. 11) The Additional Session is EU-only and offers no Language Centre exams, so an applicant entering through it must already hold recognised certificates and cannot attend the September intensive language courses.
